newsitem.title: USA: Republic Industries acquiring more new car dealerships.
newsitem.headline: Republic Industries acquiring more new car dealerships.

text.p: Republic Industries Inc., continuing to add new dealerships to its rapidly growing used car chain, said Tuesday it would acquire Maroone Automotive Group, which operates several major new and used car outlets in Florida and New York, for about $200 million in stock.

The announcement came just a day after Republic said it would pay about $100 million to acquire Grubb Automotive Inc., which owns and operates six new and used vehicle dealerships in Arizona and Texas.
Maroone Automotive, which is privately held, owns and operates seven new and used vehicle dealerships, six in southern Florida, where Republic is based, and one in Buffalo, N.Y.

"The Maroone Automotive group will be a key component of our vehicle retailing strategy," said Republic Chairman Wayne Huizenga, who built Blockbuster Video into a national force and is now building a national chain of used car megastores called AutoNation USA.

"As part of this strategy, we plan to have new vehicle stores in markets where we are developing AutoNation USA," Huizenga said. "Maroone Automotive will enable us to add more major automotive brands as a complement to our used car megastores in South Florida."
Maroone Automotive owns the fourth-largest Chevrolet store, third-largest Dodge location and largest Isuzu franchise in the United States. It also owns Ford and Oldsmobile franchises.
As part of the deal, Michael E. Maroone, who heads the chain of dealerships that his father developed, will become president of Republic's new-car division.
The transaction includes the acquisition of Maroone's existing dealerships, new locations and franchises under development, and all related real estate and other ancillary businesses.
The closing of the transaction is subject to customary conditions, including approval by appropriate manufacturers and regulatory agencies, as well as by the Republic board.
The transaction will be accounted for as a pooling of interests, which will make it tax-free for Maroone's owners.
Republic Industries, based in Ft. Lauderdale, Fla., also operates in the solid waste and electronic security services industries.
Republic's stock gained $1.125 to $37 in early trading on the Nasdaq market.
